values.STACK: a Rust Cargo workspace for peer-to-peer clipboard, notification and file sync over Tailscale, with a platform-independent core, strict clippy, arch-lint crate boundaries and behaviour-named tests
FINGERPRINT_FILES: - Read `arch-lint.toml` (scopes and the `core-stays-platform-independent` deny list) and `clippy.toml` (thresholds)
values.ARCH_VOCAB: crates, `bifrost-core` (platform independent), the daemon `bifrostd`, per-OS adapters, repository tools, value objects, errors per module boundary
ARCH_RULES: - `bifrost-core` uses no platform crate (Windows, macOS, Android, Wayland, D-Bus bindings) and neither the daemon nor the tools
- `bifrostd` is built on `bifrost-core`; the tools under `tools/` check the workspace and never use the product crates
- A new platform crate is added to the deny list in `arch-lint.toml` in the pull request that introduces it
- The final crate layout and the per-OS adapter template are decided by spike #23 and written into `AGENTS.md` section 2 by #50; until then those are the only rules
DOMAIN_EXAMPLES: - Action verbs: "sync the clipboard", "pair a device", "mirror a notification", "send a file"
- Integration surfaces: Tailscale, Wayland and Hyprland, D-Bus, the Android, macOS and Windows adapters
values.DATAFLOW_EXAMPLE: platform adapter reports a clipboard change → `bifrost-core` sync engine → transport over Tailscale → peer daemon → peer platform adapter
ENTITY_RULES: - **Primitives are wrapped**: domain fields are newtypes, never bare `String`, integers or `bool` (`AGENTS.md` section 3 forbids boolean flags in signatures and structs).
- **Fields are private** (`-`), behaviour is public (`+`); no needless `pub` (`unreachable_pub` is forbidden).
- **Errors are types**: one `<<error>>` enum per module boundary, never a leaked foreign error.
- **Platform concepts stay out of `bifrost-core`**: a need of the core that only a platform can meet is a `<<trait>>` owned by the core and implemented by an adapter.
- **No floating point or unchecked integer arithmetic** in modelled fields.
APPROACH_SECTIONS: - [Value objects, invariants, state; key decisions and rationale]
- [Which crate owns what; traits declared in the core; how the daemon wires adapters]
- [Error enums per boundary; adapter to core mapping; what the user sees]
- [Adapters per OS, Tailscale, wire protocol; or "None"]
- [Behaviour-named tests per use case with fakes; a check's test pair]
STRUCTURE_OUTPUT: 1. `bifrost-core` — [new or changed value objects, traits, errors]
3. New crate dependencies: [crate, version, which crate uses it] or "None"
1. [`arch-lint.toml` scopes or deny-list lines to add or confirm]
values.OPERATION_ORDER: value objects and errors in `bifrost-core` → traits → use cases → adapters → daemon wiring → boundaries (`arch-lint.toml`) → docs → verify
OPERATIONS_EXAMPLE: 4. Behaviour: [methods, each with purpose and signature in prose]
2. Contract tests: [cases every adapter must pass]
4. Tests: [behaviour tests with an in-memory fake]
2. Error mapping: [platform error to core error]
### 6. Docs - `AGENTS.md` section(s) and, for a user-facing change, `README.md`
values.NORMS_LINES: Error handling / Naming / Logging / Documentation / Tests
SAFEGUARD_LINES: 2. Architecture: [crate boundaries; `arch-lint.toml`; no platform crate in the core]
3. Lints: [clippy and arch-lint pass with zero exceptions; `clippy.toml` thresholds]
4. Errors: [exact error enum variants and Display messages]
6. Security & privacy: [no secrets, tokens or synced content in logs]
7. Tests: [required behaviour tests; a new check has a failing and a passing test]
CODING_NORMS: - Newtypes with validating constructors; private fields; no needless `pub`
- Functions of at most 25 lines and 3 parameters, cognitive complexity at most 8, no boolean flags in signatures or structs, identifiers of three or more characters
- No `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!`, `todo!`, `unimplemented!`, `unreachable!`, indexing, string slicing or `as` conversions; no `unsafe`; no floating point or unchecked integer arithmetic
- One error type per module boundary, never a leaked foreign error
- `///` docs on public items and module docs; `Debug` on public types
- No printing or `dbg!` outside tests; never log secrets, tokens or clipboard, notification or file content
TEST_NORMS: - Test names say the behaviour, for example `a_use_of_a_platform_crate_in_core_fails`
- Tests run with `cargo nextest` and doc tests with `cargo test --doc`; both are in `just test`
- A check that fails a build ships with a test that fails on a violation and passes on a clean input, plus a test that runs it on the real workspace
values.CHECK_DESC: fmt-check (rustfmt and rumdl), clippy with -D warnings, cargo deny, arch-lint, nextest and doc tests
values.COMMIT_REF: `Closes #<n>` in the pull request, `(#<n>)` in each commit title (`Refs #<n>` for an epic)
values.GATE_RULE: `AGENTS.md` section 5: an issue with Effort 5 or more follows SPDD, and its analysis is the gate (no code before the analysis exists). An issue below Effort 5 has no SPDD artifacts. Effort is read at triage, and the analysis may raise it.
values.GATE_READ: find the Project titled "Bifrost" with `gh project list --owner jaoppb --format json`, then `gh project item-list <number> --owner jaoppb --limit 1000 --format json`, and take the Effort of the item for `<n>`; a missing `project` scope is fixed with `gh auth refresh -s project`
values.TAXONOMY_RULE: `AGENTS.md` section 7 requires exactly one `type:` label, at least one `area:` label and one milestone (and a parent, epics excepted). Check them with `gh issue view <n> --json labels,milestone`.
values.EXEMPT_RULE: `AGENTS.md` section 5: spikes (the `type:spike` label) are exempt from SPDD.
values.BOARD_START: Starting the analysis moves the card to In progress by hand (`just project-sync` never does that).
values.BOARD_AFTER: run `just project-check`, then `just project-sync`, after opening the PR (→ In review) and after the merge (→ Done).
values.DEPS_RULE: Shared dependency versions live in `[workspace.dependencies]`, a 0.x dependency that breaks between releases is pinned exactly, and `just deny` (licenses, advisories, bans, sources) must pass (`AGENTS.md` section 3).
